speaker: Unknown
en: Last month, A16Z American Dynamism Films screened short films about three portfolio companies.
zh: 上个月，A16Z American Dynamism Films 放映了关于三家投资组合公司的短片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ulysses builds mission-critical underwater robots, Mariana Minerals applies modern technologies to the critical mineral sector, and Radiant seeks to mass-produce nuclear microreactors.
zh: Ulysses 构建关键任务水下机器人，Mariana Minerals 将现代技术应用于关键矿物领域，Radiant 致力于量产微型核反应堆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, all three films are available on A16Z's YouTube channel.
zh: 现在，这三部影片都可以在 A16Z 的 YouTube 频道上观看。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before you check them out, today's episode highlights previous appearances by all three company founders.
zh: 在你去观看之前，今天的节目重点介绍了这三位公司创始人的过往登场。

speaker: Unknown
en: First up, Ulysses Willowryan joined MTS last April after their latest fundraise.
zh: 首先，Ulysses 的 Willowryan 在他们最新一轮融资后于去年四月加入了 MTS。

speaker: Unknown
en: Super exciting.
zh: 超级令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for the audience, what exactly is Ulysses and what do you do?
zh: 那么对于观众来说，Ulysses 到底是什么，你们是做什么的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, at Ulysses we're building the ocean company.
zh: 是的，在 Ulysses 我们正在构建这家海洋公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Essentially, if you have a difficult or tough problem to solve in the surface or subsea domain, we build autonomous robots that solve that problem.
zh: 本质上，如果你在水域或水下领域有一个困难或棘手的问题要解决，我们会构建能解决该问题的自主机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the platform is basically autonomous surface vehicles combined with autonomous underwater vehicles built to be kind of cheap enough that you can kind of deploy them at scale over large swathes of the ocean, that they can work together autonomously to kind of solve, yeah, some of the most critical tasks in our oceans.
zh: 你知道，该平台基本上是自主水面航行器与自主水下航行器的结合，构建得足够便宜，以至于你可以大规模地将其部署在广阔的海域上，它们可以自主协同工作来解决，是的，一些我们海洋中最关键的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what kind of critical tasks?
zh: 比如什么样的关键任务？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, sure.
zh: 是的，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have three main verticals that we operate in.
zh: 我们在三个主要垂直领域运营。

speaker: Unknown
en: We actually began, you know, because we were very interested in problems in the world of kind of conservation and nature.
zh: 我们实际上开始，你知道，是因为我们对自然保护领域的问题非常感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was kind of the first use case we built our autonomous and water vehicle, Mako 4.
zh: 那是我们构建我们的自主水面航行器 Mako 4 的第一个用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that is doing things like mapping coral reefs, mapping undersea ecosystems, using the vehicles to collect seeds and replant them in new locations.
zh: 所以这就是做像绘制珊瑚礁地图、绘制水下生态系统地图、使用航行器收集种子并将它们重新种植到新位置这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was kind of like a first and early use case.
zh: 那是第一个也是早期的用例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, you know, after that, we kind of...
zh: 然后，你知道，在那之后，我们有点……

speaker: Unknown
en: got pulled into our second vertical, which is what we call the commercial vertical.
zh: 被拉入了我们的第二个垂直领域，我们称之为商业垂直领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: The commercial vertical, we're doing things like inspecting offshore wind platforms, inspecting subsea cables, doing repairs on undersea infrastructure.
zh: 在商业垂直领域，我们正在做像检查海上风电平台、检查海底电缆、修复水下基础设施这样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's billions of dollars of assets in the Earth's oceans owned by energy companies.
zh: 地球的海洋中有数十亿美元的资产归能源公司所有。

speaker: Unknown
en: and telecoms companies.
zh: 和电信公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So just basically, you know, protecting them and that sort of thing and keeping them up to date.
zh: 所以基本上就是，你知道，保护它们及诸如此类的事情，并保持它们的最新状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, now actually as well, you know, we got pulled into the world of events by the US Navy.
zh: 然后，你知道，实际上现在也是，你知道，我们被美国海军拉入了事件的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: They came to us when they heard about our underwater vehicle.
zh: 当他们听说我们的水下航行器时，他们找到了我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were extremely impressed with some of the specs and very dissatisfied with a lot of the existing options given by the primes.
zh: 他们对一些规格印象非常深刻，并且对主承包商提供的许多现有选项非常不满意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mako, our underwater vehicle, is truly best in class for its form factor, the small to medium size.
zh: 我们的水下航行器 Mako 就其外形尺寸而言，即中小尺寸，确实是同类中最好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for them, they're interested in things like how can we find and remove mines?
zh: 所以对他们来说，他们对像我们如何找到并清除水雷这样的事情感兴趣？

speaker: Unknown
en: How can we gather intelligence under waters?
zh: 我们如何在水下收集情报？

speaker: Unknown
en: And how can we do other relevant, important tasks like protecting ports, harbors, critical infrastructure, that sort of thing.
zh: 以及我们如何做其他相关的、重要的任务，比如保护港口、码头、关键基础设施，诸如此类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: All done off the same core tech platform, but...
zh: 所有这些都基于同一个核心技术平台完成，但是……

speaker: Unknown
en: it's pretty valuable and can be used across each.
zh: 它非常有价值，并且可以跨越每一个领域使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the kind of similarities maybe to think about is people are building general purpose robotic form factors on land in the form of the humanoid.
zh: 也许可以考虑的一个相似之处是，人们正在陆地上构建以人形机器人形式的通用机器人外形尺寸。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can't just take a humanoid robot and throw it into the ocean.
zh: 你不能直接拿一个人形机器人把它扔进海洋里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just doesn't work that way.
zh: 它不是那样运作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to have something that maybe looks a bit more like a fish or a shark.
zh: 你必须拥有某种可能看起来更像鱼或鲨鱼的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the kind of platform that we're hoping to build for the ocean.
zh: 那就是我们希望为海洋构建的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you ever played Subnautica?
zh: 你玩过《潜渊症》吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I haven't, but I have heard of it.
zh: 我没玩过，但我听说过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's incredible.
zh: 真是不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like Subnautica is like Ulysses the game.
zh: 看起来《潜渊症》就像是游戏版的 Ulysses。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also haven't played it.
zh: 我也没玩过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't really play that many video games, but it's just like, it's a game where you, I believe, are a guy controlling a submarine that's going around an alien ocean and exploring things and solving technical problems and fighting sea monsters.
zh: 我其实不怎么玩电子游戏，但这就像，这是一个，我相信，你是一个家伙控制潜艇在异星海洋中四处航行并探索事物和解决技术问题以及与海怪战斗的游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, pretty much the average day in the life for a Ulysses forward deployed engineer.
zh: 是的，基本上就是 Ulysses 前线部署工程师的平均一天生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you think about why there are so relatively few ocean companies?
zh: 你认为为什么海洋公司相对如此之少？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, there's a billion space companies, there's a billion satellite companies, there's a billion robot companies, but so few of them seem to be focused on the ocean.
zh: 你知道，有十亿家太空公司，有十亿家卫星公司，有十亿家机器人公司，但其中很少有专注于海洋的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And is it just because space and land robots are sexier somehow?
zh: 这仅仅是因为太空和陆地机器人在某种程度上更性感吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think part of it is kind of a narrative.
zh: 是的，我认为其中一部分是叙事的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's like a different narrative for the ocean and it's not, you haven't got this kind of like, you know, inspirational framing of like the iconic images of like Apollo and SpaceX, you know, rockets launching again and you haven't had a company like doing the kind of SpaceX version of like, let's make this domain sexy again for the ocean.
zh: 对于海洋有一种不同的叙事，它不是，你没有得到这种，你知道，像 Apollo 和 SpaceX 那样的标志性图像的鼓舞人心的框架，你知道，火箭再次发射，你还没有像一家做海洋领域的 SpaceX 版本那样的公司，让我们让这个领域再次性感起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it's worth considering
zh: 但我认为值得考虑

speaker: Unknown
en: going back and looking at like history to understand that like this is an anomaly, a historic anomaly that we haven't been as obsessed with exploring the oceans.
zh: 回过头来看看历史，以理解这是一种反常，一种历史反常，我们竟然如此着迷于探索海洋。[[52]] 有史以来，人类总是梦想着，你知道，海洋生物，海洋探险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Since the dawn of time, mankind has like dreamed of, you know, sea creatures, expeditions at sea.
zh: 自古以来，人类就像梦想着，你知道，海洋生物，海洋探险。

speaker: Unknown
en: Moana.
zh: 《海洋奇缘》(Moana)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it was the pinnacle of like frontier spirit and exploration for most of humanity's history.
zh: 是的，那是人类大部分历史中边疆精神和探索的巅峰。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it seems around the kind of 60s and 70s, we kind of forgot about it.
zh: 然后似乎在 60 年代和 70 年代左右，我们有点把它忘记了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like at that point in the 60s when the US was really kind of, you know, just so optimistic and so ambitious.
zh: 但就像在 60 年代的那个时候，当美国真的非常，你知道，如此乐观和如此雄心勃勃的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, a lot of people fail to realize or actually, you know, forget.
zh: 很多人没有意识到或者实际上，你知道，忘记了。

speaker: Unknown
en: is that exploring the Earth's oceans was a co-equal ambition as going to the moon.
zh: 探索地球海洋是与登月同等的雄心。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the 1964 World's Fair, GM had this ride, Futurama 2, that 26 million people saw this.
zh: 在 1964 年世界博览会上，通用汽车(GM)有一个游乐项目，Futurama 2，有 2600 万人看过这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was like a lunar base on one side of it, but then you also had a subsea hotel called Hotel Atlantis that had ocean floor oil rigs and submarine trains bringing critical minerals to shore.
zh: 它的一侧有一个月球基地，但还有一个名为亚特兰蒂斯酒店的深海酒店，有海底石油钻塔和潜水火车将关键矿物运送到岸上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you had a resort down there where people could look around JFK,
zh: 那里有一个度假村，人们可以四处看看，JFK(JFK/肯尼迪)，

speaker: Unknown
en: you know, commissioned this plan that was effectively like the undersea equivalent for...
zh: 你知道，委托制定了这个计划，这实际上是……的深海同等物

speaker: Unknown
en: the undersea equivalent of kind of like a space program.
zh: 相当于某种太空计划的深海同等物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he tripled funding year over year to explore the Earth's oceans.
zh: 他将探索地球海洋的资金逐年增加了两倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we had people living on the sea floor.
zh: 然后我们有了在海底生活的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Navy had this program called Sea Lab, right?
zh: 海军有这个叫 Sea Lab 的项目，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they were sending people down to live at the bottom of the ocean.
zh: 他们把人送下去住在海底。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then very unfortunately, we had the death of one of the members, Barry Cannon, one of the explorers kind of down there.
zh: 然后很不幸，我们其中一名成员去世了，Barry Cannon，一名在那里探险的成员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that combined with the redirecting of a lot of the Navy's kind of budget and towards things like focusing on Vietnam.
zh: 加上海军预算的重新分配，比如专注于越南战争之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And...
zh: 以及……

speaker: Unknown
en: other kind of priorities led to a neglect in funding and resources to go and look at the underwater domain.
zh: 其他优先事项导致了对去探索水下领域的资金和资源的忽视。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, the underwater domain in the Cold War became very heavily classified.
zh: 此外，冷战时期的水下领域变得高度机密。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's been books released in the last decade or two talking about the hunt for Red October.
zh: 过去一二十年出版了一些书籍，谈论《猎杀红色十月》(the hunt for Red October)。

speaker: Unknown
en: These kind of books that are talking about all these crazy things the US subs were doing in this era.
zh: 这些书谈论美国潜艇在这个时代做的所有疯狂事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was all...
zh: 那都是……

speaker: Unknown
en: very classified stuff.
zh: 非常机密的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They couldn't talk about it publicly, right?
zh: 他们不能公开谈论它，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So you had this like insane engineering, the same exploration going on undersea, but it was totally classified and we couldn't speak about it publicly.
zh: 所以你拥有这种疯狂的工程技术，同样的探索在海底进行，但这完全是机密的，我们不能公开谈论它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also like Jacques Cousteau, the biggest cultural icon for it, he was real about exploration and then he kind of pivots more to like conservation.
zh: 还有像雅克·库斯托(Jacques Cousteau)，最大的文化偶像，他致力于探索，然后他转向更多地关注保护。

speaker: Unknown
en: So...
zh: 所以……

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this cultural shift, there's this classification, and as a result, 50 years later, we're still working with the same tools in the ocean.
zh: 有这种文化转变，这种机密化，结果 50 年后，我们仍在使用海洋中的同样工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's exactly this kind of exploration spirit, this desire to conquer this great blue frontier that we're trying to reignite and be that SpaceX for the ocean that young kids are dreaming about being in.
zh: 正是这种探索精神，征服这个蔚蓝边疆的愿望，正是我们试图重新点燃的，并成为海洋的 SpaceX，这是年轻孩子们梦想成为的。

speaker: Unknown
en: you know, aquanauts as well as, like, astronauts and, you know, going to these frontiers.
zh: 你知道，海洋宇航员(aquanauts)以及像宇航员(astronauts)一样，你知道，去这些边疆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because when you get into the engineering of it, it's gnarly stuff.
zh: 因为当你进入它的工程领域时，那是棘手的东西(gnarly stuff)。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it's really gnarly stuff to kind of make vehicles that can work in the deeps, work in the depths.
zh: 就像，这是非常棘手的东西(gnarly stuff)，要制造能在深海、在深处工作的载具。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's, like, arguably more difficult than, like, a lot of the, like, making a vehicle that can survive in space.
zh: 就像，可以说比制造许多能在太空中生存的载具更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a lot more things trying to take you out down there.
zh: 而且有更多的东西试图在那里干掉你。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, yeah, there's a cultural kind of and military reasons why we don't really have a generation of kids thinking of building ocean companies.
zh: 我认为，是的，有文化上的和军事上的原因，为什么我们真的没有一代孩子想着建立海洋公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this makes me wonder, what is China doing in oceans?
zh: 这让我想知道，中国在海洋方面在做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, yeah, this is, you know, kind of the long and the short of it is in the undersea domain, it still remains a domain in which like the U.S. can create a decisive advantage, right?
zh: 我是说，是的，这，你知道，归根结底就是在水下领域，它仍然是一个美国可以建立决定性优势的领域，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like on shipbuilding, like, you know, China is, you know, by far and away ahead, right?
zh: 似乎在造船方面，像，你知道，中国是，你知道，遥遥领先，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Building hundreds of ships per annum to the U.S. building kind of single digit ships, right?
zh: 每年建造数百艘船，而美国建造个位数的船，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: In aerial drones, it's like they're producing tens of millions.
zh: 在空中无人机方面，他们生产了数千万。

speaker: Unknown
en: The US is maybe making a single-digit million, if even.
zh: 美国可能在制造个位数的百万，如果有的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in the autonomous underwater vehicle, undersea drone space, we're looking at single-digit thousand autonomous underwater vehicles or underwater drones made every year.
zh: 但在自主水下航行器、水下无人机空间，我们正在看每年制造数千个自主水下航行器或水下无人机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And hundreds of them are made in China and hundreds of them are made in the US.
zh: 其中数百个是在中国制造的，数百个是在美国制造的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's not a total disparity here.
zh: 所以这里并没有完全的差距。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're on the same kind of order of magnitude.
zh: 我们处于相同的数量级。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the undersea domain is definitely a domain in which the U.S. could create an advantage.
zh: 所以水下领域绝对是一个美国可以建立优势的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, that being said, China is moving forward itself on a lot of undersea initiatives.
zh: 话虽如此，中国自身正在推进许多海底倡议。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they're building, they just released this kind of submarine-sized autonomous underwater vehicle that has a range that can extend 18,000 kilometers.
zh: 他们正在建造，他们刚刚发布了一种潜艇大小的自主水下航行器，其航程可达 18,000 公里。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, it could potentially reach the coastline of the United States.
zh: 所以，你知道，它有潜力到达美国的海岸线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's obviously a massive threat.
zh: 这显然是一个巨大的威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: They also have cable cutting tools and they can operate at like a depth of like 4,000.
zh: 他们还有剪缆工具，并且可以在大约 4,000 的深度运作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a really serious like asymmetric threat that they have on the U.S. now.
zh: 所以这对美国来说，他们现在确实拥有一种非常严重的不对称威胁。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not many capabilities the U.S. has in this kind of size variant.
zh: 美国在这种尺寸变体上没有太多能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in addition to that, they're also building what they call like an underwater gray wall of sensors across the Indo-Pacific.
zh: 除此之外，他们还在建造所谓的横跨印太地区的水下灰色传感器墙。

speaker: Unknown
en: These would be sensors that you put down, pretty low power draw, and they can sense maybe submarines or other things moving and they're networked.
zh: 这些是你放置的传感器，功耗很低，它们可以感知潜艇或其他东西的移动，并且是联网的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it gives them this kind of undersea kind of GPS or navigating capability, which would obviously be very useful to them in the context of a war.
zh: 这赋予了他们这种海底 GPS 或导航能力，这在战争背景下显然对他们非常有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they're not like leaps and bounds ahead of where the US is.
zh: 但他们并没有领先美国一大截。

speaker: Unknown
en: At least, you know, we're looking at opening,
zh: 至少，你知道，我们正着眼于开设，

speaker: Unknown
en: a facility next year or beginning to kind of like break ground on it next year, that facility alone would, you know, two to three X like international supply of autonomous underwater vehicles.
zh: 一个设施，明年或明年开始破土动工，仅那个设施就能，你知道，将自主水下航行器的国际供应量提高两到三倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, obviously all of that will be built in the United States.
zh: 而且，你知道，显然所有这些都将在美国建造。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, undersea dominance is definitely within reach for the US versus China.
zh: 所以，你知道，与中国相比，美国实现海底主导权绝对是触手可及的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.
zh: 有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: So especially in the last decade or so, there's been this idea of seasteading, especially among libertarians.
zh: 特别是在过去十年左右，一直有这种海上家园的想法，尤其是在自由意志主义者中。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Peter Thiel was really into this.
zh: 你知道，Peter Thiel 对此非常热衷。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Zuckerberg was into this.
zh: 我认为 Zuckerberg 也对此感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea being, you know, if you can't create libertarian utopia in any existing country, and there's no frontier left because all the land is gone, you can build libertarian utopia in the middle of the ocean.
zh: 这个想法是，如果你无法在任何现有国家建立自由意志主义乌托邦，而且没有最后的疆界了，因为所有陆地都没了，你可以在海洋中央建立自由意志主义乌托邦。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or just forgetting about the libertarian valence, just like having Cuban habitation in the middle of the ocean.
zh: 或者暂时忘掉自由意志主义的倾向，就像只是在海洋中央有 Cuban 居住地。

speaker: Unknown
en: So do you think this is a good idea?
zh: 那么你认为这是一个好主意吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it tractable at all?
zh: 这完全可行吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think it's definitely a good idea.
zh: 是的，我认为这绝对是个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the intellectual merit of the idea is great.
zh: 我认为这个想法的理论价值很高。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think like, yeah, like Thiel kind of speaks about this, you know, the sovereign individual is probably one of the first books that really kind of coined, I think, a lot of these ideas back in the 90s.
zh: 我想，是的，就像 Thiel 谈到这个，你知道，《主权个体》大概是首批真正创造了这些想法的书籍之一，我想是在 90 年代。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, in a world that is like increasingly regulated and burdened and shackled, you know, man desires for the freedom and therefore he can go to sea and build these, you know, kind of habitations out there and be...
zh: 但是是的，在一个监管日益增加、负担日益沉重、受到束缚的世界里，你知道，人类渴望自由，因此他可以去海洋并在那里建造这些居住地，并且成为……

speaker: Unknown
en: you know, doesn't have to worry about regulation or red tape.
zh: 你知道，不必担心监管或繁文缛节。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could be a great place to do some interesting things in biotech and longevity and other kind of forms of experimentation where people want to, they want to voluntarily like take maybe treatments or something like that, but the government here won't let them.
zh: 对于生物技术、长寿和其他形式的实验来说，这可能是一个做些有趣事情的好地方，在这些地方人们想要自愿接受某种治疗或类似的东西，但这里的政府不允许他们这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's like a lot of merit in a lot of that.
zh: 所以我认为这其中有很多优点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also like just the sheer kind of mass.
zh: 而且就像仅仅是因为这种巨大的规模。

speaker: Unknown
en: if we're to get the most out of the ocean and the resources that it provides to us and also to bring some kind of order to it being a very disordered place.
zh: 如果我们要充分利用海洋及其提供给我们的资源，并给这个非常无序的地方带来某种秩序。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we do need to put habitations out there.
zh: 我认为我们确实需要在那里建立居住地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like more of the important work is going to be done by robots in the future out there.
zh: 未来更多的重要工作将在那里由机器人完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think we will want to have humans out there and I think you could build some really nice settlements out there.
zh: 但我认为我们会希望人类在那儿，我认为你可以在那里建造一些非常好的定居点。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think, so I think the idea of sea setting has its merit.
zh: 但我认为，所以我认为海上家园这个想法有其优点。

speaker: Unknown
en: for sure, but I think what was wrong, what they didn't have at the time, were the tools and technology to build it.
zh: 当然，但我认为错误在于，他们当时所没有的，是建造它的工具和技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a good idea, but it was too early because the technological enablers weren't doing it.
zh: 这是一个好主意，但为时过早，因为技术推动因素当时还没到位。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what do you need if you want to build out at sea?
zh: 那么如果你想在海上建造，你需要什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, you definitely want internet.
zh: 好的，你肯定需要互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: Starlink changes the game.
zh: Starlink 改变了游戏规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the first time ever, you can actually have a habitation out there that can be connected to the rest of the world through something like Starlink.
zh: 有史以来第一次，你实际上可以在那里拥有一个居住地，可以通过像 Starlink 这样的东西连接到世界其他地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, you want to have logistics freshened up pretty frequently.
zh: 好的，你希望物流更新相当频繁。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, trying to get a big container ship or someone like that to come out and stop off in your location and drop something there, maybe not that realistic.
zh: 同样，试图让一艘大型集装箱船或类似的东西出来，在你的地点停靠并把东西扔在那里，可能不太现实。

speaker: Unknown
en: But again, if you have a Poseidon Aerospace autonomous cargo plane that can come out and refuel you every two weeks or week with new supplies, that's great.
zh: 但同样，如果你有一架 Poseidon Aerospace 自主货机可以出来，每隔一周或一周给你补充新物资，那就太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, you want to do maintenance on your floating rig.
zh: 好的，你希望对你的钻井平台进行维护。

speaker: Unknown
en: This floating rig right there, things are breaking.
zh: 那个浮动钻井平台，东西正在坏掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: divers are super expensive okay that could like pretty much bankrupt you if things are breaking and you can't fix them in time okay you have your Ulysses autonomous underwater robots that go in and like fix the cables underneath it and tie these things down or whatever so you're starting to see the preparation of tools now that I think that can actually reduce the cost of preparation down such that the benefits do outweigh the costs in something like seasteading.
zh: 潜水员非常昂贵，好的，如果东西坏了而你不能及时修复，那可能会让你破产，好的，你有你的 Ulysses 自主水下机器人进去，修复下面的电缆，把这些东西固定下来或做其他什么，所以你开始看到工具的准备现在，我认为这实际上可以将准备成本降低，以至于在像海上家园这样的事情中，收益确实超过了成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: You also need energy generation at sea.
zh: 你还需要在海上发电。

speaker: Unknown
en: Solar has come on like leaps and bounds in the last few decades.
zh: 太阳能在过去几十年中突飞猛进。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's possible.
zh: 所以这是可能的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're also seeing interesting advances in ocean geothermal, or basically just like taking advantage of natural heat in the ocean to generate energy with pantalasa generating wave energy.
zh: 我们也看到了海洋地热能方面的有趣进展，或者基本上就像是利用海洋中的自然热能来产生能源，pantalasa 产生波浪能。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have CarPowerShip who developed these modular kind of floating power stations that you can put on a ship so that it can be brought out to locations.
zh: 我们有 CarPowerShip，他们开发了这些模块化的浮动发电站，你可以把它放在一艘船上，这样它就可以被运送到各个地点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, the power, the logistics, the data problem, the kind of like operators and maintenance, these are all problems that are now starting to be solved for the first time.
zh: 所以是的，电力，物流，数据问题，还有那种操作和维护，这些都是现在第一次开始解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, C-setting, I would love to see it come back.
zh: 所以是的，C-setting，我很乐见它回归。

speaker: Unknown
en: Interesting.
zh: 有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've had a lot of incidents in the last few years of oil pipelines and internet connectivity cables being cut, you know, often as an act of deliberate sabotage.
zh: 所以在过去几年里，我们发生了许多石油管道和互联网连接电缆被切断的事件，你知道，通常是作为一种蓄意破坏的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you defend against these?
zh: 你们如何防御这些？

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like you just have a lot of potential attack surface and it's tough to defend.
zh: 看起来你有很多潜在的攻击面，而且很难防御。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, you need a combination of, you know, sensing, sensor nodes like placed along all this infrastructure and you need to make, they need to be really cheap.
zh: 是的，你需要结合，你知道，感知，沿着所有这些基础设施放置的传感器节点，你需要制造，它们需要非常便宜。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that gives you like your kind of, your eyes and ears, you can tell, but you need to also be able to intervene and actually protect.
zh: 这给了你那种，你的眼睛和耳朵，你可以分辨，但你还需要能够进行干预并真正保护。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's where the robotics and like underwater drones like the Mako would come into it.
zh: 这就是机器人和像 Mako 这样的水下无人机派上用场的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you need those two kind of combination of those two things.
zh: 所以你需要这两者的结合。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you need the ability to refuel them at sea as well.
zh: 然后你还需要能够在海上为它们补充燃料。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you need something like Leviathan, the autonomous surface vehicle, that can recover them, recharge them, connect them to the internet so they can relay that data back.
zh: 所以你需要像 Leviathan 这样的东西，这种自主水面航行器，它可以回收它们，给它们充电，将它们连接到互联网，这样它们就可以将这些数据传回。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you need all of the stack to be made super cheap, such that you can deploy them over a massive scale.
zh: 然后你需要整个堆栈都变得超级便宜，以便你能够大规模部署它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is exactly the lens that we brought to building these things.
zh: 而这正是我们制造这些东西的视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you want to buy an autonomous...
zh: 如果你想购买一个自主的……

speaker: Unknown
en: underwater vehicle from one of the primes or something like that to do these interventions and protect your cables today.
zh: 水下航行器，来自一家主要承包商或类似的机构，来进行这些干预并保护你今天的电缆。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're paying like in the order of millions of dollars and they don't come with a launch and recovery system to recharge them and they don't have native integration into seedbed sensors to protect the cables.
zh: 你要支付大约数百万美元，而且它们不带有发射和回收系统来为它们充电，而且它们没有与海床传感器进行原生集成以保护电缆。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, that's why we're kind of taking this full stack from sensors to surface to subsea approach.
zh: 所以是的，这就是为什么我们采取这种从传感器到海面再到海底的全栈方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, these are all very much things that we're kind of thinking about.
zh: 是的，这些都是我们非常正在思考的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nice.
zh: 很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you are also, in addition to being the co-founder and CEO of Ulysses, the secretary of the Hamilton Society, which is one of my favorite things in SF, actually.
zh: 所以你也是，除了是 Ulysses 的联合创始人和 CEO 之外，还是 Hamilton Society 的秘书，这实际上是我在 SF 最喜欢的事情之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I go to most or all of the Hamilton Society meetings.
zh: 我会参加大部分或所有的 Hamilton Society 会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: For the audience, it's this debate society.
zh: 对于听众来说，这是一个辩论社团。

speaker: Unknown
en: They meet in this church in the Richmond like once a month.
zh: 他们每个月在 Richmond 的一座教堂里聚会一次。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very formal.
zh: 非常正式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You are required to wear a suit and tie.
zh: 你被要求穿西装打领带。

speaker: Unknown
en: if you're a man, and black tie if you're a woman.
zh: 如果你是男性，如果你是女性则穿黑领结。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you are not wearing a suit and tie, they will just not let you in.
zh: 如果你没有穿西装和领带，他们就不会让你进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's great.
zh: 这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it has this like real atmosphere of kind of professionalism and dignity and sort of old academia aesthetics.
zh: 所以它有一种真正的专业、庄重和那种旧学院派美学的氛围。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how did that whole thing come about?
zh: 那整个事情是如何发生的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, a part of it was, you know, I moved to San Francisco and I came from Ireland where, you know, we love, you drink pints of Guinness and like that's our social, you know, we go to the pub, you know, we hang out, you know, groups and none of my friends worked in tech.
zh: 是的，其中一部分是，你知道，我搬到了旧金山，我来自爱尔兰，你知道，我们热爱，你喝品脱的吉尼斯黑啤酒，就像那是我们的社交，你知道，我们去酒吧，你知道，我们闲逛，你知道，一群人，我的朋友里没有人在科技行业工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then like being, you know, dropped into San Francisco where nobody drank, everyone took off their shoes.
zh: 所以然后像是，被，你知道，扔进旧金山，那里没人喝酒，每个人都脱掉了鞋子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were in like someone's like extremely brightly lit like living room.
zh: 你就像是，在某人那里的，极其明亮的，客厅里。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then like everyone was talking about their stupid startup.
zh: 然后每个人都在谈论他们愚蠢的初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was like, this is like hell.
zh: 我就像是，这就像是地狱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to talk about these things.
zh: 我不想谈论这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't want to be in this like environment.
zh: 我不想待在这个像是环境里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to have a drink.
zh: 我想要喝一杯。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to have like, you know, fun.
zh: 我想要像是，你知道，乐趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want the room to be a bit darker.
zh: 我想要房间稍微暗一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then like Hamilton was like the opposite of all the things.
zh: 然后 Hamilton 就像是所有事情的对立面。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't talk about your startup.
zh: 你不谈论你的初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You keep your shoes on.
zh: 你穿着鞋子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You dress nicely.
zh: 你穿得体面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you talk about like an important problem of the day.
zh: 你谈论像是当今的一个重要问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, so it was like, that was my own kind of personal motivation.
zh: 而且，你知道，所以这就像是，那是我自己的个人动机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was kind of like a lot of the motivation.
zh: 这在很大程度上就是很多动力所在。

speaker: Unknown
en: of co-founders that we started with.
zh: 就是我们开始时拥有的那些联合创始人的动力。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in addition to that, there was this kind of bigger belief that San Francisco is, in my opinion, the most important city in the world.
zh: 但除此之外，还有一个更大的信念，即旧金山在我看来是世界上最重要的城市。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it doesn't have social institutions that match its ambitions in the material world.
zh: 但它没有与其在现实世界的野心相匹配的社会机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: It doesn't have places where ideas are formed, where people can debate.
zh: 它没有形成思想的地方，没有人们可以进行辩论的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just really people shouting at each other on Twitter.
zh: 真的就只是人们在 Twitter 上互相大喊大叫。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you look at any great...
zh: 如果你看看任何伟大的……

speaker: Unknown
en: moment of kind of immense you know wealth creation or otherwise we've had these social institutions where people could network and connect and like for converge on like what is truth of what this community should advance and seek to advance and you know together you know the UK kind of had like Oxford Union and these set of like members clubs in places like London the you know we had the Pacific Union Club you have other kind of members clubs on the east coast as well in places like New York from the industrial revolution but you know today like
zh: 那些巨大的你知道的财富创造或其他时刻，我们都有这些社会机构，人们可以在那里建立联系，并像是汇聚于这个社区应该推进什么的真理，并寻求推进，你知道在一起，你知道英国某种程度上有像是牛津协会和这些像是伦敦等地的一套会员俱乐部，你知道我们有太平洋联盟俱乐部，你在东海岸也有其他类似的会员俱乐部，在像是纽约这样的地方，来自工业革命时期，但你知道今天像是

speaker: Unknown
en: you know, this physical place instantiation of it does not exist.
zh: 你知道，这种物理场所的具象化并不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Hamilton's society was kind of conceived in that vein as well.
zh: 所以 Hamilton's society 也就是在那个脉络下构思出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And yeah, looking to draw on the kind of heritage of places like Oxford Union, how they run their debates.
zh: 是的，并希望借鉴像是牛津协会这类地方的遗产，借鉴他们如何运作辩论的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, yeah.
zh: 所以，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much cultural impact do you think it has had so far?
zh: 你认为它到目前为止产生了多大的文化影响？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it is, in its early days of kind of cultural impact, I think it has been good at like, you know, like I think one example is like the billionaire tax.
zh: 我认为它处于文化影响的早期阶段，我认为它在像是，你知道像是我认为一个例子就是像是亿万富翁税。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anybody who was at that debate has come away with an actually way more high fidelity understanding of like why a billionaire tax is like very bad, right?
zh: 任何参加过那场辩论的人都带着一种实际上更高保真度的理解离开，关于为什么亿万富翁税是非常糟糕的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Beforehand, it was like the extent of which people really had seriously engaged in it was like...
zh: 在此之前，人们真正认真参与它的程度就像是……

speaker: Unknown
en: maybe you were just like billionaires are good or something like that.
zh: 也许你只是觉得亿万富翁是好的或者类似的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You didn't understand why the mechanics of it or the mechanics of what they were actually proposing and why specifically those were bad and what maybe an alternative might be if you still wanted to generate tax revenue through wealth.
zh: 你不理解为什么它的机制或者他们实际提议的机制为什么具体是糟糕的，以及如果你仍然想通过财富产生税收收入，也许替代方案可能是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: All these points on the ladder that I was talking about are points that were brought up that night.
zh: 我刚才谈到的梯子上的所有点，都是那天晚上提出的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we literally had Trey Stephens, a real life billionaire, founder of Underworld, debating the two guys who wrote the policy.
zh: 而且我们真的请到了 Trey Stephens，一位现实生活中的亿万富翁，Underworld 的创始人，与撰写该政策的两个人进行辩论。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think everyone came away with it like, oh wow, okay, we now understand specifically why it's bad such that the 600 people who attended and the 400 people who voted against the billionaire tax at that night's debate can now bring that into their own relevant communities when they meet people who are like, hey, we should do a billionaire tax.
zh: 我认为每个人都带着像是，噢哇，好吧，我们现在具体理解了为什么它是糟糕的，这样那天晚上参加的 600 人和投票反对亿万富翁税的 400 人现在可以将其带入他们自己的相关社区，当他们遇到像是，嘿，我们应该征收亿万富翁税的人时。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they have the talking points that they can go straight to right now.
zh: 而且他们拥有现在可以直接使用的谈话要点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's probably that ripple down effect that when people go back to the communities they have that now as well.
zh: 所以这可能是那种连锁反应效应，当人们回到他们的社区时，现在也有了这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Similarly, when we have debates on things like Christianity or religion or, you know,
zh: 同样，当我们对像是基督教或宗教或，你知道，

speaker: Unknown
en: gender relations or other things like people can like bring the talking points into their own life so maybe a difficult one to measure like specifically oh we'll be led to this but I think it's only a matter of time that you start to see kind of concrete impacts and in the culture.
zh: 性别关系或其他类似事情进行辩论时，或者人们可以将谈话要点带入他们自己的生活，所以也许是一个很难具体衡量的，像是哦我们将导致这个，但我认为开始看到具体的文化影响只是时间问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I hope you're right.
zh: 我希望你是对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's definitely a good cultural institution.
zh: 我认为这绝对是一个好的文化机构。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you scheduled the next debate yet?
zh: 你已经安排下一场辩论了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not yet.
zh: 还没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have some exciting potential speakers in the lineup.
zh: 我们有一些令人兴奋的潜在演讲者在阵容中。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're always trying to go one level up and quality is better than quantity for us.
zh: 我们总是尝试更上一层楼，对我们来说质量胜于数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have some interesting ones in the work and we'll be sharing more on Twitter in the coming weeks.
zh: 所以我们有一些有趣的正在筹备中，我们将在未来几周在 Twitter 上分享更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cool.
zh: 很酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: So back to Ulysses, what is the ultimate vision for the company?
zh: 所以回到 Ulysses，这家公司的最终愿景是什么？

speaker: Unknown

en: five years is Indonesian kind of like production capacity has scaled to the point where it's now something like 70% of global nickel comes out of Indonesia.
zh: 五年里发生的事情是印尼的生产能力已经扩大到了某种程度，现在全球大约 70% 的镍产自印尼。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of that was on the back of like meaningful investment from China to be able to kind of expand production capacity in Indonesia and then also do more of the downstream processing in Indonesia.
zh: 其中很多是在中国大量投资的支持下，得以扩大印尼的生产能力，然后在印尼进行更多的下游加工。

speaker: Unknown
en: And nickel goes into everything that is specialty alloys, anything that needs high temperature or corrosion resistance, and also is kind of the unsung hero of high-energy batteries, where these lithiated transition metal oxides, which are high nickel.
zh: 镍用于所有特种合金，任何需要高温或耐腐蚀性的东西，也是高能量电池的无名英雄，其中这些锂化过渡金属氧化物是高镍的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Manganese is important.
zh: 锰很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: Manganese goes into a lot of alloys and also goes into batteries.
zh: 锰用于很多合金，也用于电池。

speaker: Unknown
en: The uranium, if fission is going to continue to grow and we're going to continue to deploy more nuclear capacity in the U.S., then uranium is going to happen, is going to be needed.
zh: 铀，如果裂变将继续增长，我们将继续在美国部署更多核电容量，那么铀将会发生，将会被需要。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a long list.
zh: 这是一个很长的清单。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, the rare earths, you know, they're important, obviously.
zh: 而且,你知道,稀土,你知道,它们很重要,显然。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are omnipresent in, like, everything that we use.
zh: 它们无处不在,就像,在我们使用的所有东西里。

speaker: Unknown
en: But they show up as, like, a relatively small kind of, like, on a volume basis when you look at kind of the stack of metals that we need to mine.
zh: 但当你审视我们需要开采的金属堆栈时,就体量而言,它们表现为一种相对较小的种类,就像。

speaker: Unknown
en: And where, you know, the...
zh: 而且那里,你知道,那个……

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely we need a ton of, like, process innovation in how rares are refined.
zh: 毫无疑问,我们在稀土如何提炼方面需要大量的,就像,工艺创新。

speaker: Unknown
en: Solvent extraction circuits are kind of like the status quo.
zh: 溶剂萃取电路是目前的现状。

speaker: Unknown
en: They, you know, the chemical intensity is high and the recoveries are relatively low.
zh: 它们,你知道,化学强度很高,而回收率相对较低。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the know-how is kind of like highly penetrated or highly concentrated in China.
zh: 而且诀窍就像是被高度渗透或高度集中在中国。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mm-hmm.
zh: 嗯。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it is a little bit of a frothy market right now.
zh: 但这目前确实是一个有点泡沫的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so being a diversified minerals company kind of enables us to pick our spots in areas where it makes sense.
zh: 因此,成为一家多元化矿产公司使我们能够在有意义的领域挑选我们的切入点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like these things still do move on commodity cycles and you actually want to be building infrastructure at the bottom of commodity cycles, not at the top of commodity cycles.
zh: 就像这些东西仍然会随大宗商品周期波动,而你实际上想要在大宗商品周期的底部建设基础设施,而不是在顶部。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, it's the Warren Buffett quote of, you know, invest when there's blood in the water.
zh: 你知道,这是沃伦·巴菲特的名言,你知道,在血溅街头时投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you want to be coming into metals when they are at like this trough, really, where no one is investing in them.
zh: 就像你想要在金属处于低谷时进入,真的,那时没人投资它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They still have like a macro long-term critical point.
zh: 它们仍然具有宏观长期关键点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Lithium is like exactly in this position right now.
zh: 锂就完全处于这个位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why we're focused on lithium.
zh: 这就是我们要专注于锂的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: Copper just has this macro trend that is pretty hard to ignore.
zh: 铜具有一种很难忽视的宏观趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're just going to need an insane amount of copper.
zh: 我们将需要大量的铜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Copper grids are going down globally, which means that our ability to extract copper from those ores is going to get...
zh: 铜品位在全球范围内正在下降,这意味着我们要从这些矿石中提取铜的能力将变得……

speaker: Unknown
en: harder and harder to extract copper from those ores.
zh: 从这些矿石中提取铜变得越来越难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's where, you know, the plant OS side of things, we have like a high degree of confidence that we'll be able to step in and kind of like optimize the refining circuits to still be able to extract copper from these lower grade ores without seeing meaningful kind of cost increases.
zh: 这就是,你知道,工厂操作系统方面的事情,我们有很高的信心,我们能够介入并优化提炼回路,以便仍然能够从这些低品位矿石中提取铜,而不会看到有意义的成本增加。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everyone knows, you know, people here, it takes forever to get a mine started.
zh: 所以大家都知道,你知道,这里的人,开始一个矿山需要很长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how many new greenfield mines we've developed in the United States in the last decade.
zh: 我不知道我们在过去十年里在美国开发了多少新的绿地矿山。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not many.
zh: 不多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know Australia and Canada have been able to do this faster, which is interesting.
zh: 而且我知道澳大利亚和加拿大能够做得更快,这很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't know Canada for moving quickly.
zh: 你不会认为加拿大行动迅速。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are some of the bottlenecks there?
zh: 那里的一些瓶颈是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: What does America need to do to accelerate this as one of these companies trying to not only mine but also refine in the United States?
zh: 作为一家不仅试图在美国开采而且还要在美国提炼的公司,美国需要做什么来加速这一点?

speaker: Unknown
en: What needs to be done?
zh: 需要做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think one thing that folks don't always see is actually the permitting requirements for exploration.
zh: 是的,我认为人们并不总能看到的一件事实际上是勘探的许可要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there is like, if you are exploring over on federal land, if you're exploring over more than a five acre parcel, you have to submit like a plan of record or plan of operations that needs to be approved by the BLM before you can start to expand, like expand and explore over a larger piece of land.
zh: 所以就像,如果你在联邦土地上勘探,如果你勘探超过五英亩的土地,你必须提交一份记录计划或运营计划,需要 BLM 批准,你才能开始扩展,就像扩展并在更大的土地上勘探。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the, like, bringing down the permitting thresholds and the permitting burden associated with exploring, like, that is why we have such a small, like, relatively small rare earth resource.
zh: 所以,降低与勘探相关的许可门槛和许可负担,这就是为什么我们的稀土资源如此之少,就像相对较小的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, it's not because there isn't, like, the U.S. has tons of natural resources.
zh: 这就像,并不是因为,就像,美国拥有大量的自然资源。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the, like...
zh: 而且,就像……

speaker: Unknown
en: the kind of like USGS estimate for U.S., like the U.S. Reserve on rare is just picking on that.
zh: 就像 USGS 对美国的估计,就像美国的稀土储量只是以那个为例。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like that is tied to a lack of exploration activity, not necessarily fundamentally like a lack of kind of like geologic presence.
zh: 这归因于缺乏勘探活动,不一定根本上是缺乏地质存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we haven't looked for it.
zh: 而且我们没有寻找过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we haven't, either we haven't looked for it or it's.
zh: 是的,我们没有,要么我们没有寻找过它,或者它是。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, well, it's hard to find in like high concentrations that are mineable, which we're trying to kind of like drop the percentage requirement that makes something economical.
zh: 是的,嗯,很难找到高浓度的可开采矿石,我们正试图降低使某事经济化的百分比要求。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it's also, there's just a lot of like kind of like permitting burden to be able to actually go and deploy drill rigs to go and actually explore.
zh: 而且,还有,有很多许可负担,以便能够真正去部署钻机去真正勘探。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then...
zh: 然后……

speaker: Unknown
en: There's definitely a, the government currently is doing a good job of kind of highlighting the importance of the minerals industry.
zh: 肯定有一个,政府目前在很好地强调矿产工业的重要性方面做得很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're definitely seeing like a little bit of a tone shift over the last 20 years that is much more supportive.
zh: 而且你肯定在过去 20 年里看到了一点语气转变,这更加支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's way more tailwinds when it comes to kind of like making mining possible.
zh: 当谈到使采矿成为可能时,有更多的顺风。

speaker: Unknown
en: be viewed in a more positive light and a critical light.
zh: 被以更积极的光和关键的光看待。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that will help to solve some of the talent pool problem where people that are, you know, awesome, they want to go build things.
zh: 这将有助于解决一些人才库问题,那些,你知道,很棒的人,他们想去建设东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't want to go and like work on a project that kind of sits around for five years and maybe gets permitted and maybe doesn't.
zh: 他们不想去在一个项目上工作,项目闲置五年,也许获得许可,也许没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like they want to go work on hard problems where they can see the impact of the work that they're doing.
zh: 就像他们想去从事那些可以看到他们所做工作影响的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if we're getting in the way of...
zh: 所以如果我们阻碍了……

speaker: Unknown
en: of enabling projects to get built, like, that is actually a major deterrent for talent because they won't actually see what they're, like, the, like, output of their work.
zh: 阻碍了项目的建设，这实际上是对人才的一个巨大阻碍，因为他们实际上看不到他们，呃，工作的产出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I, you know, I think the permitting requirements broadly for going from a discovery to an operating asset
zh: 然后，我，你知道，我认为总体上对于从发现到运营资产的许可要求

speaker: Unknown
en: There should be a big focus on kind of efficiency in reviewing environmental permits.
zh: 应该重点关注审查环境许可的效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: There should be a big focus on kind of like streamlining those workflows and the back and forth between kind of like field offices and state offices from the BLM, just focusing on the federal side of things.
zh: 应该重点关注简化那些工作流程，以及 BLM 的现场办公室和州办公室之间的来回沟通，只关注联邦方面的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the way that projects get permitted right now is you'll throw your environmental assessment over the table.
zh: 因为目前项目获得许可的方式是你把你的环境评估扔到桌子对面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they'll go and they'll divvy it up between a whole bunch of experts that they are like kind of consultants that they bring in to review the permit.
zh: 然后他们会把它分给一群专家，他们像是他们带进来审查许可的顾问。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they'll get back to you eventually at some point.
zh: 他们最终会在某个时候回复你。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there isn't a lot of visibility into like how they are progressing with reviewing the permit applications.
zh: 但是对于他们如何推进审查许可申请，并没有太多的可见性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And discussions are getting more...
zh: 讨论正变得越来越……

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, there's been definitely a change with the new administration where there's a little more accountability on the permitting offices.
zh: 同样，随着新一届政府的到来，肯定发生了一些变化，许可办公室有更多的问责制。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's tons of room for making those reviews more efficient.
zh: 但是在提高那些审查效率方面还有很大的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, LLMs will make it more efficient.
zh: 同样，LLM 会让它更有效率。

speaker: Unknown
en: We just need to kind of penetrate that side of the federal bureaucracy and enable people to review things faster.
zh: 我们只需要渗透联邦官僚机构的那一面，并让人们能够更快地审查事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: What else?
zh: 还有其他的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Aside from kind of permitting efficiency, what are other things that if, you know, if you could send a list of recommendations to the government for what they should do to support the U.S. mining industry, what would be your top three?
zh: 除了许可效率，如果你可以给政府发送一份建议清单，说明他们应该做什么来支持美国采矿业，你的前三条建议会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think supporting the demand side is probably like the biggest lever.
zh: 是的，我认为支持需求端可能是最大的杠杆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you want to mobilize kind of private capital into the sector, having some level of support on the demand side is major.
zh: 如果你想要调动私人资本进入该行业，在需求端有一些支持是至关重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's offtake agreements with floor pricing.
zh: 所以这就是带有底价的承购协议。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, they did this just now with MP Materials.
zh: 你知道，他们刚刚对 MP Materials 做了这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that, you know, ideally provides some stability on the revenue side of things so that investors like that there's trillions of dollars of capital kind of like dry powder just sitting around waiting to be deployed.
zh: 而且，理想情况下，这在收入方面提供了一些稳定性，以便投资者喜欢那里有数万亿美元的资本只是作为干粉闲置等待部署。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is historically kind of avoided the mining industry because of the market price uncertainty.
zh: 历史上，它一直回避采矿业，因为市场价格的不确定性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so as soon as you provide, it's a commodity cycle.
zh: 所以一旦你提供，这是一个大宗商品周期。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, what if you're building at the wrong time?
zh: 如果你在错误的时间建设怎么办？

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, the infrastructure funds are not the ones that are here to play, like, be intelligent about the commodity price cycle.
zh: 而且，你知道，基础设施基金不是那些在这里玩弄，聪明地应对大宗商品价格周期的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, they're looking for annuity type returns.
zh: 他们寻找的是年金类型的回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so those folks would mobilize if there were more demand side support from the government, either providing price floors or fixed pricing for critical minerals that, you know, you're trying to incentivize more production of in the U.S.
zh: 所以如果有政府更多的需求端支持，这些人就会动员起来，无论是提供底价还是为你试图在美国激励更多生产的关键矿物提供固定定价。

speaker: Unknown
en: you know, participating in the capital stack is important.
zh: 参与资本结构是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think lowering the hooks or the, you know, the extra burden that comes in with receiving government funds is important.
zh: 我认为降低钩子或者你知道接收政府资金带来的额外负担是重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like some government agencies probably have more leeway to do that.
zh: 就像一些政府机构可能有更多的余地来做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the DOD, obviously, again, just did this big deal with MP materials.
zh: 像 DOD，显然，再次，刚刚与 MP Materials 做了这笔大交易。

speaker: Unknown
en: and actually, like, went all the way to kind of participating in the cap table or as an equity holder.
zh: 实际上，甚至一路参与到了资本表或作为股权持有者。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when you receive federal funds from the DOE or if you receive federal funds from, like, you know, on the debt side of things, from EXIM...
zh: 但是当你从 DOE 接收联邦资金，或者如果你从，你知道，在债务方面，从 EXIM 接收联邦资金……

speaker: Unknown
en: it comes with some like additional burden sometimes.
zh: 有时它会带来一些额外的负担。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like if you are building on state land and you just need a state permit and then you bring in federal funds, you now bump your permitting requirement to a federal level permit.
zh: 就像如果你在州土地上建设，只需要州许可，然后你引入了联邦资金，你现在就把你的许可要求提升到了联邦级别的许可。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's the NEPA process, which, you know, again, the NEPA process wouldn't be as burdensome if there was some more efficiency on the permitting side of things.
zh: 这就是 NEPA 流程，你知道，同样，如果在许可方面有一些效率，NEPA 流程就不会那么繁重。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mineral deposits, specifically like high-grade mineral deposits, don't obey borders.
zh: 矿床，特别是高品位矿床，不遵守边界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there a broader international strategy here?
zh: 这里有更广泛的国际战略吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, I would love to think we can mine and refine everything in the United States, but obviously there's a lot, Australia, Canada, Latin America.
zh: 我的意思是，我很想认为我们可以在美国开采和提炼所有东西，但显然有很多，澳大利亚，加拿大，拉丁美洲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Africa.
zh: 非洲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Africa, underwater, seafloor.
zh: 非洲，水下，海底。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the overall strategy in your mind?
zh: 在你心目中，总体战略是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, we're starting in the U.S. because it's closer to home and we're focused on developing a platform that we can scale off of.
zh: 是的，我们从美国开始，因为它离家更近，我们专注于开发一个我们可以扩展的平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at no point have we told ourselves that the U.S. is kind of like the only, the sole focus.
zh: 但是从来没有告诉过我们自己，美国是唯一的，唯一的焦点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you have to be able to like bolster the company to be able to operate internationally if you want to be able to scale beyond kind of like the resource base that the U.S. has like available today.
zh: 你必须能够加强公司以便能够国际运营，如果你想要扩展超出美国今天可用的资源基础。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so more exploration is going to happen in the U.S. We'll probably discover more resources and like that pool will grow over time of projects that we can build in the U.S.
zh: 所以更多的勘探将在美国进行。我们可能会发现更多的资源，而且那个项目池会随着时间增长，我们可以在美国建设。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yes, we are absolutely going to expand overseas and underwater maybe.
zh: 但是是的，我们绝对会向海外扩张，也许还有水下。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we look back a decade from now, what's the single clearest indicator that Mariana has achieved what it set out to do?
zh: 当我们十年后回顾时，Mariana 已经实现了它所要做的最清晰的指标是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We won't be as worried about our ability to secure the critical minerals that we want to secure because we will have kind of rebuilt...
zh: 我们不会太担心我们确保我们想要确保的关键矿物的能力，因为我们将已经重建……

speaker: Unknown
en: and established an entity, ideally, that is able to go across borders, to your point, and build these projects cost-effectively, time-effectively, and responsibly, ultimately.
zh: 并建立了一个实体，理想情况下，能够跨越边界，正如你所指出的，并在最终以具有成本效益、时间效益和负责任的方式建设这些项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason that we are so panicked about it right now is because we have fundamentally lost the ability to build large-scale infrastructure, and we have lost the ability to operate complex minerals plants.
zh: 我们现在对此如此恐慌的原因是我们从根本上丧失了建造大规模基础设施的能力，我们也丧失了运营复杂矿物工厂的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what we have lost.
zh: 这就是我们失去的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we need to build that back.
zh: 我们需要重建那一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to build 10 projects in 10 years.
zh: 我们想在 10 年内建造 10 个项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those projects will be an increasing scale over time, but the work will not be done in 10 years.
zh: 这些项目随着时间的推移规模会不断扩大，但这工作不会在 10 年内完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I think will have demonstrated that the 10-year mission will have been accomplished, other than building those 10 plants, is that we will no longer be as worried about our fundamental capability to go and build this complex infrastructure.
zh: 我认为除了建造那 10 家工厂之外，能证明这 10 年使命已经完成的是，我们将不再像以前那样担心我们建造这种复杂基础设施的基本能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We will have unlocked it.
zh: 我们将解锁它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Last up, Doug Berdauer, founder and CEO of Radiant, alongside Drew Baglino, founder and CEO of Heron, joined me and A16Z general partner Aaron Price-Wright to discuss nuclear's role in rebuilding America's energy infrastructure.
zh: 最后，Radiant 创始人兼 CEO Doug Berdauer，以及 Heron 创始人兼 CEO Drew Baglino，与我和 A16Z 普通合伙人 Aaron Price-Wright 一起讨论了核电在美国能源基础设施重建中的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about the moment, the insight, the why now that led you to start your respective companies.
zh: 谈谈那个时刻、那个洞察、那个「为什么是现在」，引导你们各自创办了自己的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Doug, let's start with you and Radiant.
zh: Doug，让我们从你和 Radiant 开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh man, it's a fun story.
zh: 噢伙，这是个有趣的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was at SpaceX for 12 years.
zh: 所以我在 SpaceX 待了 12 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: I joined in 2007.
zh: 我在 2007 年加入。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I joined when they had two failed rockets, no successful rockets.
zh: 所以我加入的时候，他们有两枚失败的火箭，没有一枚成功的火箭。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I got to work on the first ones that worked.
zh: 所以我得以参与第一批能工作的火箭。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're like, this is the company to be at.
zh: 你会觉得，这就是那个该待着的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I just wanted to work on an important mission.
zh: 是的，我只是想从事一项重要的使命。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I really just cared, can I like polish one stone of this like great big pyramid that is like some lifetime achievement for someone else even, right?
zh: 我真的只是在乎，我能不能打磨这块巨大金字塔上的一块石头，这甚至可能是别人一辈子的成就，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I wanted.
zh: 这就是我想要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, I joined, I did that.
zh: 所以是的，我加入并做到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did the first two Falcon 9s, did the ground system for it entirely, which involved all the permitting also.
zh: 我做了前两枚 Falcon 9，并负责了它的地面系统的全部工作，这涉及所有的许可。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is like launching a rocket from a military base.
zh: 所以这就像是从军事基地发射火箭。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of like regulatory stuff there.
zh: 那里有很多监管方面的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: your first foray into the marketing wilderness.
zh: 你第一次涉足监管荒野。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not to eat up all the time.
zh: 别占用所有时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I worked on like the first rocket with legs called Grasshopper back in 2011.
zh: 你知道，我在 2011 年参与了第一枚带腿的火箭，被称为 Grasshopper 的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was a four person team really designing, building the whole team, the whole thing.
zh: 这真的是一个四人团队在设计、建造整个团队、整个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were reporting directly to Elon, like just Elon, two of us, four, and then building the whole thing.
zh: 而且我们直接向 Elon 汇报，只有 Elon，我们中的两个，然后是四个，然后建造整个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was awesome because we did really well.
zh: 这太棒了，因为我们做得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got lucky a lot of times, but we made a rocket that flew and landed on legs.
zh: 我们很多时候运气很好，但我们制造了一枚能飞并且用腿着陆的火箭。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I did all the weird Elon side projects and ideas.
zh: 然后我做了所有那些奇怪的 Elon 副业项目和想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Hyperloop, when he got really serious, I got tapped into that and into the Boring Company and then Mars Colony Design.
zh: 所以 Hyperloop，当他变得非常认真的时候，我也被卷入了其中，还有 The Boring Company，然后是火星殖民地设计。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in doing the Mars Colony Design, I was looking at how do you take Starship there, make fuel from what's on Mars, make fuel from the ice that's there.
zh: 在做火星殖民地设计时，我在研究如何把 Starship 送到那里，利用火星上的东西制造燃料，利用那里的冰制造燃料。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you do that, you need megawatts of power.
zh: 如果你那样做，你需要数兆瓦的电力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was trying to do it with solar and getting totally stuck and showing Elon these plans that were like four miracles we need on a single mission.
zh: 我试图用太阳能来做，结果完全卡住了，并向 Elon 展示了这些计划，上面写着我们需要在单次任务中实现四个奇迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it was just ridiculous.
zh: 这简直太荒谬了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Elon was like, you probably should look at nuclear.
zh: 所以 Elon 说，你应该看看核电。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's really the jumping off point, right?
zh: 那真的是起点，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I started to learn.
zh: 我开始学习。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then three years later, I left to go run.
zh: 三年后，我离职去经营它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I founded Radiant and left to go run it.
zh: 我创立了 Radiant 并离职去运营它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And really trying to make mass-producible, portable micro-reactors.
zh: 真正致力于制造可大规模生产的、便携式的微型反应堆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not for space, but currently we're focused on a trailer-sized thing.
zh: 不是为了太空，但目前我们专注于一个拖车大小的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But also needed in space.
zh: 但太空也需要它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right, yeah.
zh: 对，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I do eventually want to do products for space, but we've got to have customers.
zh: 所以我最终确实想为太空制造产品，但我们必须要有客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've got to have funds that are actually there.
zh: 我们必须要有实际到位的资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: Doug, it seems like the tide turned on nuclear a few years ago in that, you know, more and more people started to realize the, you know, the importance and criticality of it.
zh: Doug，似乎几年前核电的形势发生了转变，你知道，越来越多的人开始意识到它的重要性和关键性。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is sort of the progress that we've made as an industry?
zh: 作为行业，我们取得了哪些进展？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, what have we achieved and, you know, what are the biggest bottlenecks remaining in terms of, you know, really making progress as a country?
zh: 你知道，我们取得了什么成就，以及，你知道，作为一个国家，在真正取得进展方面，剩下的最大瓶颈是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a good question.
zh: 这是一个好问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a bunch of fun ways to answer it.
zh: 我想有一堆有趣的方式来回答它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the one thing I like to say, it sounds a little sensationalist, is that there is no nuclear industry.
zh: 我的意思是，我喜欢说的一件事，这听起来有点耸人听闻，那就是没有核工业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: but it's really true.
zh: 但这确实是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we're kind of, it's almost like we're getting excited about flight before Kitty Hawk, right?
zh: 你知道，我们有点像是，这几乎就像我们在 Kitty Hawk 之前对飞行感到兴奋一样，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: To a certain degree.
zh: 在某种程度上。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a really coming very soon deadline.
zh: 有一个真正即将到来的非常紧迫的最后期限。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of companies, a lot of little nuclear startups have actually been given access to fuel and facilities and just expedited support from the subject matter experts required to regulate to make sure that these are going to be safe tests.
zh: 许多公司，许多小型核能初创公司实际上已经获得了燃料和设施的使用权，以及来自主题专家的加速支持，这些专家需要进行监管以确保这些将是安全的测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so by July 4th, several companies will have reactors built that go critical that are fundamentally new designs, completely new and from scratch, but it hasn't happened yet.
zh: 所以到 7 月 4 日，几家公司将建造出达到临界的反应堆，这些设计从根本上说是全新的，完全是从头开始的，但这还没发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it just feels like a little bit of cart before the horse.
zh: 所以感觉有点像本末倒置。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that worry you at all?
zh: 这让你担心吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Not too much.
zh: 不太担心。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I've been doing nuclear, well, thinking about it since 2016, but I founded Radiant in 2019 and then for a year just learned how to do reactor design and then raised money in 2020.
zh: 你知道，我一直在做核能，嗯，从 2016 年就开始思考了，但我在 2019 年创立了 Radiant，然后花了一年时间学习如何进行反应堆设计，然后在 2020 年筹集了资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'd never founded a company before, never intended to really do that, and I kind of slow rolled into it.
zh: 而且我以前从未创立过公司，从未真正打算这样做，我有点缓慢地进入了这个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could have tried to go much faster.
zh: 我本可以试着走得更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I've stayed totally committed to just building.
zh: 但我完全坚持致力于单纯的建造。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually the funny thing is like in 2020, I said in 2026, I will put a full scale reactor and get it critical and get it up to full power.
zh: 实际上有趣的是，在 2020 年，我说在 2026 年，我将放置一个全尺寸的反应堆并使其达到临界状态，并将其提升到全功率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're on schedule to do that, which is kind of wild.
zh: 而我们正按计划做到这一点，这有点疯狂。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not like that was really the actual plan, but it was just, I was resilient to all the challenges that were put in the way.
zh: 这并不是说那真的是实际的计划，但这只是，我对所有摆在面前的挑战都有韧性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We are now the only reactor permitted to, of these new reactors to go to full power.
zh: 我们现在是唯一被允许达到全功率的新反应堆。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a lot of others are getting to critical.
zh: 所以很多其他的反应堆将达到临界状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: which doesn't mean you get to high temperatures or high power.
zh: 这并不意味着你会达到高温或高功率。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those things are very challenging on all the parts in the system, right?
zh: 而这些事情对系统中的所有部件来说都是非常具有挑战性的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And they require careful consideration of the thermal gradients and the alloys, right?
zh: 它们需要对温度梯度和合金进行仔细的考虑，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You need high strength materials to do that.
zh: 你需要高强度材料来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's really exciting, but we're like not quite there yet.
zh: 所以这真的很令人兴奋，但我们还没有完全做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think if we're doing the same discussion next year, it's going to be dramatically different because we're going to be able to point at all these different designs, what you could do with them.
zh: 我认为如果我们明年进行同样的讨论，情况将发生巨大变化，因为我们能够指出所有这些不同的设计，你可以用它们做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the products like nuclear reactors as products has never been seen before.
zh: 我认为像核反应堆作为产品这样的产品以前从未见过。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are always usually these giant mega projects where you dig a huge hole in the ground and you take five to 10 years or up to 15 for the slower, the bad projects out there.
zh: 通常总是有这些巨大的大型项目，你在地上挖一个巨大的洞，你需要 5 到 10 年，或者对于那里较慢的糟糕项目来说甚至长达 15 年。

speaker: Unknown
en: But reactors that can just come ours, you know, we're targeting one per week coming off of a production line from our Tennessee facility, which is an 80 acre site we just signed for in October, not even a year ago.
zh: 但是反应堆就这样来了，我们的，你知道，我们的目标是每周从我们的田纳西州工厂的生产线产出一个，那是我们在不到一年前的 10 月刚签下的 80 英亩的场地。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to tie back into the grid because I was just, I had some interesting thoughts and we really, our product is for off the grid, right?
zh: 我想联系回电网，因为我刚才，我有一些有趣的想法，我们的产品确实是针对离网的，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So megawatt reactor on a trailer and you can, we build in our factory, we drive it or fly it to where the customer wants it to go and then turn it on within like 48 hours.
zh: 所以拖车上的兆瓦级反应堆，你可以，我们在工厂里建造它，我们把它开车或飞机运到客户想要它去的地方，然后在大约 48 小时内打开它。

speaker: Unknown
en: We go, you know, wheels stop moving and then we go to power on your site in that amount of time.
zh: 我们，你知道，轮子停止移动，然后我们在那段时间内为你的站点供电。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it lasts five years, which is like a full oil tanker worth of diesel equivalent.
zh: 然后它持续五年，这就像相当于一整艘油轮的柴油量。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's 2 million gallon diesel equivalent.
zh: 这相当于 200 万加仑的柴油。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's sort of an unbelievable thing where you can grow the grid or put a microgrid anywhere, but it's a totally different problem, I think, from the grid itself is civilization, right?
zh: 所以这是一件不可置信的事情，你可以在任何地方扩大电网或放置微电网，但我认为这与电网本身是文明这一完全不同的问题，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Electric power is civilization.
zh: 电力就是文明。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go and there's sockets and you pop something into them and you just get power, that's very well developed.
zh: 如果你去了那里，有插座，你把东西插进去，你就得到了电力，这是非常发达的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's civilization and that's using electricity to do what you could otherwise only do with human muscle or animal muscle.
zh: 那就是文明，那就是利用电力来做否则你只能用人力或畜力才能做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: How should we think about how microreactors fit within the broader energy landscape?
zh: 我们应该如何思考微型反应堆如何融入更广泛的能源格局？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they compete with large centralized plants?
zh: 它们与大型集中式电厂竞争吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do they complement them?
zh: 它们是互补的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they serving in different categories of demand?
zh: 它们服务于不同类别的需求吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: How should we think about it?
zh: 我们应该如何思考这个问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so they're definitely an off-grid product.
zh: 是的，所以它们绝对是一种离网产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they don't at all compete with larger reactors.
zh: 所以它们根本不与大型反应堆竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really, if you have time to dig a big hole in the ground and put a reactor in that way, then you can do a larger reactor, maybe five or ten times as big as the one megawatt size that we're looking at, and it's going to win on economics.
zh: 真的，如果你有时间在地上挖个大洞然后把反应堆那样放进去，那你就可以做一个更大的反应堆，也许是我们正在看的一兆瓦大小的五到十倍，而且它会在经济性上胜出。

speaker: Unknown
en: It definitely should.
zh: 肯定应该如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're already using one of the fanciest forms of fuel, and that is so that we can set it up anywhere and have it not be a risk to people or facilities nearby.
zh: 我们已经在使用最高级的一种燃料形式了，这样我们就可以在任何地方设置它，并且让它对附近的人员或设施不构成风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we don't compete at all with those things.
zh: 所以我们根本不与那些东西竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the ways I like to talk about this is you can run a diesel generator or you can run a nuclear reactor and you're really deciding between those two things.
zh: 我喜欢谈论这个问题的方式之一是，你可以运行柴油发电机，或者你可以运行核反应堆，而你真的就是在那两样东西之间做决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we don't beat like super cheap diesel.
zh: 而我们赢不了那种超级便宜的柴油。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we beat diesel at like 650 a gallon, that kind of a number.
zh: 我们是在柴油大约 650 美元一加仑这种数字上赢过柴油。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's where our initial customers need to be.
zh: 所以这就是我们最初的客户需要所在的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you go start looking at what people pay for diesel and what they pay on the edges, not on like the center of the bell curve, the average for like a country or an area, like you look at the tough,
zh: 但如果你开始看看人们为柴油付了多少钱，以及他们在边缘地区付了多少钱，而不是像钟形曲线的中心，也就是一个国家或地区的平均值，就像你看那些艰苦地区，

speaker: Unknown
en: they're paying a lot.
zh: 他们付得很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's plenty of customers out there.
zh: 所以外面有很多客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some examples, I think.
zh: 我想有些例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, like $10 a gallon is the average in Hong Kong.
zh: 哦，比如 10 美元一加仑是香港的平均水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think like Iceland and Scandinavia, Northern Europe, those regions are like $7, $8, $9 per gallon for a whole country, actually.
zh: 我认为像冰岛和斯堪的纳维亚，北欧，这些地区的价格是每加仑 7、8、9 美元，实际上是针对整个国家。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like...
zh: 所以像……

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very easy to see.
zh: 很容易看出来。

speaker: Unknown
en: The market is massive.
zh: 市场是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And islands.
zh: 还有岛屿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, islands.
zh: 是的，岛屿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 绝对的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, Hawaii is pretty high electricity costs, and it's, I think, 80% diesel-powered, actually.
zh: 我的意思是，夏威夷的电费相当高，而且实际上我认为它是 80% 依靠柴油发电的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's got wind and solar that make up the remainder.
zh: 它剩下的部分由风能和太阳能组成。

speaker: Unknown
en: But yeah, you could have a cleaner form of power, right?
zh: 但是是的，你可以拥有一种更清洁的电力形式，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: No emissions.
zh: 零排放。

speaker: Unknown
en: The nuclear reactor operates and then rain, it takes it.
zh: 核反应堆运行，然后下雨，雨水把它带走。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we handle all the complexity.
zh: 我们处理所有的复杂性。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the amount of power people need, right?
zh: 但是人们需要的电力数量，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They need in the gigawatts for the grid.
zh: 他们为了电网需要吉瓦级的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we don't really do that.
zh: 所以我们并不真的做那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have the niche customers on the edge and we don't want to make...
zh: 我们在边缘地区有细分客户，我们不想制造……

speaker: Unknown
en: right, thousands and thousands of reactors.
zh: 对，成千上万个反应堆。

speaker: Unknown
en: At 50 a year, we'll have something in the range of like a thousand or two at the most.
zh: 以每年 50 个的速度，我们最多会有大约一千或两千个。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we don't consider, we don't look at it and go, hey, could we make it work for 10,000?
zh: 但我们不考虑，我们不看它然后说，嘿，我们能让它为 10,000 个工作吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's different products and we can do it at better economies.
zh: 有不同的产品，而且我们可以以更好的经济性做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a couple of ways to do it.
zh: 有几种方法可以做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we're, Radian doesn't want to dig a hole in the ground and solve that other miracle.
zh: 但是我们，Radian 不想在地上挖个洞去解决另一个奇迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's too many...
zh: 太多……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's important to be able to do it again, but it's not on us to fix it right away.
zh: 我认为能够再次做这件事很重要，但这不是我们要立即解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, serious miracles.
zh: 是的，严重的奇迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want to have too many in a startup.
zh: 你不想在一家初创公司里有太多奇迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need some.
zh: 你需要一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One miracle that leads to then a product and revenue, that's the way.
zh: 一个通向产品和收入的奇迹，这就是路径。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have time to think about another miracle.
zh: 然后你有时间思考另一个奇迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally.
zh: 完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you mentioned that we're very early in the nuclear industry.
zh: 所以你提到我们处于核工业的非常早期阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we're in pre the nuclear industry in some sense.
